title: Inconsistent Autofill Events and Missing Autofill Functionality

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Autofill can affect multiple components simultaneously. Additionally, there are inconsistent browser events around autofill. 

If you want to validate a multiple input autofill like an address you don’t want to validate 4 times (street, city, state, zip) - 4 events triggered for 4 input. If the inputs are autofilled sequentially then only the 4th event will be the value you actually want to validate and use. What you want is a single autofill event from the browser with a list of the elements and values included in the event, right?


### What solutions exist today?

One solution that I've used is setting up an interval to wait for all of the address values to change at the same time. But this only works if the browser autofills all of the fields.

### How would you solve it?

Event should include a reference (target) to the elements impacted by the autofill as well as the autofill type (address, phone, username, etc…) and values. There could be an option to preventDefault() or an option to change the values before they are applied.

Browsers could trigger a global autofill event on the document, iframe, and/or window (discuss). Should the event be on an element too? I would think not because it can get confusing when you have multiple events for what is actually a single event. There are pros and cons to having the event bubble down to the individual inputs, perhaps there should be a new event type for inputs.

### Anything else?
